description: A C# source generator that transforms ASP.NET Core API endpoints into MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools.
releaseNotes:
Breaking:
- ⚠️ McpScopeOptions.AreApiCallsInProcess is removed: a tool's API request always runs in process, through the app's own request pipeline, and the package sends nothing over the network. Remove the option from AddMcpTools; the README's "Migrating from 2.x" says what to do for each reason an app called over HTTP.
- ⚠️ McpHttpInvoker's public constructor, which built an invoker that called over HTTP, is removed. Resolve IMcpHttpInvoker from the app's services instead. To wrap it in a decorator, register the decorator over the registration AddMcpTools made, as the README shows, not by resolving IMcpHttpInvoker in its own registration, which resolves the decorator itself.
- ⚠️ services.AddHttpClient<IMcpHttpInvoker, McpHttpInvoker>(), with which tests handed the invoker a TestServer handler, now makes every tool call fail with an InvalidOperationException that says to remove it. Remove it: under WebApplicationFactory the tools run in process.
- ⚠️ The HttpClient named IMcpHttpInvoker serves only the default invoker's requests, in process, and refuses any other with an InvalidOperationException. An invoker of your own registered as a typed client with services.AddHttpClient<IMcpHttpInvoker, MyInvoker>() takes that name, so its requests no longer reach the address they name. Give its client a name of its own, as in services.AddHttpClient<IMcpHttpInvoker, MyInvoker>("MyInvoker").
- ⚠️ The invoker's HttpClient gets a primary handler that refuses every request, so a primary handler the app sets with ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler, a TestServer handler included, never gets a request. Remove it.
- ⚠️ A tool that called another server through McpTools:BaseUrl now calls the app itself, at the MCP request's host. Register an invoker of your own for that server, one that implements IMcpHttpRequestInvoker, as IMcpHttpInvoker, with a client of its own name, as the README's "Migrating from 2.x" shows. For an API that answers only at another host of the same app, as with RequireHost, set the Host header with a message handler of the invoker's client.
- ⚠️ McpTools:BaseUrl and ISelfBaseUrlProvider now only name a tool's request that has no MCP request to take its address from, such as one run outside an MCP request; that address is never called. DefaultBaseUrlProvider lost its constructor that took an IHttpContextAccessor, its error for an http:// binding off loopback and its preference for a loopback binding. Behind a TLS-terminating proxy, McpTools:BaseUrl and loopback among the KnownProxies are no longer needed.
- ⚠️ The tool's request no longer carries X-Forwarded-Proto, and comes from the MCP client's address rather than from loopback: an IP allow list that admitted it by loopback now refuses it. Admit HttpContext.IsMcpToolRequest() instead.
- ⚠️ What held the tool's request outside the app no longer does: IIS request filtering in web.config and the limits HTTP.sys takes from the registry. Kestrel's request limits and the server's MaxRequestBodySize still hold it. Hosting's EventSource counters, such as total-requests in dotnet-counters, no longer count it, and http.server.active_requests counts it with no api_to_mcp.tool_request tag to leave it out; count with http.server.request.duration.
- ⚠️ Under IIS a tool's request has no Windows user, so an action that requires Windows authentication answers 401 or 500 through a tool, where over HTTP a client with UseDefaultCredentials got the app pool's identity.
- ⚠️ A tool called in a host that has not built the app's request pipeline fails with an InvalidOperationException that says why, instead of calling over HTTP, and a host that starts without building it logs an error once it has started. Call a tool only once the app has started, with app.Run(), app.StartAsync() or WebApplicationFactory, and register no IApplicationBuilderFactory of your own after AddMcpTools.
- ⚠️ An [ApiController] action that requires a traceparent, tracestate, baggage, Correlation-Context or X-Forwarded-Proto header gets MCP009 and no tool, and a Minimal API endpoint MCP010, as the tool's request never carries one. Make the parameter optional.

Added:
- IMcpToolRequestFeature and HttpContext.IsMcpToolRequest(). A tool's request carries the feature, which no client can send, unlike X-MCP-Internal-Call, and its ToolName names the tool whose call sent the request. A rate limiter's partition, a middleware or a logger can tell a tool's request from a client's by it. The README shows a rate limiter that gives the tool's requests a partition of their own for each client: they carry the MCP request's connection, so a per-address limiter counted them against the client that still holds the MCP request.
- The tool's API request gets the logs, the span and the metrics ASP.NET Core's hosting gives a request the server receives, through hosting's own instruments: Request starting and Request finished in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics, under the RequestId and RequestPath scope; the server span Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.HttpRequestIn, a child of the tool call's, with the DiagnosticListener events that OpenTelemetry's ASP.NET Core instrumentation and Application Insights read; and http.server.request.duration and http.server.active_requests in the meter Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting, with http.route, error.type and the tags of IHttpMetricsTagsFeature. AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation() records it with no change. The span, the duration and the log scope carry api_to_mcp.tool_request = true.
- A tool's request is held to the request limits of the server the app runs on, as the same request sent to the server is. Under Kestrel, a request line over MaxRequestLineSize (8 KB) gets HTTP 414: URI Too Long, and headers over MaxRequestHeadersTotalSize (32 KB) or MaxRequestHeaderCount (100) get HTTP 431: Request Header Fields Too Large, before the API sees the request. TestServer has no limits.

Changed:
- ⚠️ The message handlers and DefaultRequestHeaders of the invoker's named HttpClient (IMcpHttpInvoker), which 2.x ran only over HTTP, now apply to every tool's request: AddHttpMessageHandler, AddStandardResilienceHandler, AddLogger, the handlers ConfigureHttpClientDefaults gives every client, as .NET Aspire's service defaults give AddStandardResilienceHandler, the handlers other packages add to every client through an IHttpMessageHandlerBuilderFilter, such as Sentry's, which by default reports each request that gets a 5xx response as an error event, and the client factory's logging. The request passes them all before the app serves it in process. A retrying handler runs a request that failed with a transient status, such as 503, through the app again, whatever its method. AddStandardResilienceHandler also cancels each attempt after 10 seconds and retries it, and fails the whole call after 30 seconds with TimeoutRejectedException, where 2.5.0 ran the request once under the client's Timeout, 100 seconds by default; and once at least 10 percent of at least 100 attempts within 30 seconds failed, its circuit breaker makes every tool call throw BrokenCircuitException for 5 seconds, healthy ones too, which the client gets as "An error occurred invoking '<tool>'.", not as an error result with the API's answer. To keep the resilience handlers ConfigureHttpClientDefaults adds off the tool's request, call services.AddHttpClient(nameof(IMcpHttpInvoker)).RemoveAllResilienceHandlers() (Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience 9.2.0 or later, experimental: EXTEXP0001). A default header never replaces Authorization, X-MCP-Internal-Call or a [FromHeader] argument, but a default Authorization now reaches the action when the MCP request has none. The client's Timeout applies as before. Code that takes AddMcpTools' handler builder filter away after AddMcpTools, as services.RemoveAll<IHttpMessageHandlerBuilderFilter>() or services.Replace(...) of a logging filter does, or registers an IHttpClientFactory of its own after it, as a test may to stub outgoing calls, gets the 2.5.0 behaviour instead: the request is served in process without the client's handlers and default headers, never through the primary handler or the app's factory, and the startup log warns and names the cause.
- ⚠️ Tool calls now show in the app's request metrics, spans and request log: request rates, latency percentiles and error rates on dashboards and alerts include each tool's API request. Filter on api_to_mcp.tool_request to leave them out.
- The log entries of the tool's request carry a SpanId of their own, with the tool call's span as their ParentId, as does the traceId of its ProblemDetails; before, they carried the tool call's. Their RequestPath includes the path base, as hosting's does, and their scope exists only while hosting's log category is on.
- A canceled tool call's request is logged and measured with the status 499 when the app had not started its response, as Kestrel records a client that went away, and its cancellation is no error.
- ⚠️ A tool call whose arguments make a request line or headers over Kestrel's limits, such as a long query string or [FromHeader] value, now gets that error result instead of reaching the API. Raise the limit in ConfigureKestrel, or send the value in the body.
- ⚠️ The tool's request body is held to the server's MaxRequestBodySize, 30,000,000 bytes by default under Kestrel, IIS and HTTP.sys, instead of no limit. A larger body gets HTTP 413 unless the action's [RequestSizeLimit] or [DisableRequestSizeLimit] lifts it.
- The tool's request keeps the percent-encoding it was sent with in its RawTarget, such as /users/a%40b, instead of one re-encoded from the decoded path.

Fixed:
- The MCP endpoint that MapMcpEndpoint maps refuses a tool's request without UseMcpLoopPrevention too (https://github.com/Kebechet/Api.ToMcp/issues/100). Before, an app without the middleware served such a request as a new MCP request inside the tool call. The middleware is still needed for an endpoint mapped with the SDK's MapMcp.
- Behind IIS out of process, every tool call got HTTP 400: Bad Request since 2.4.0, unless AreApiCallsInProcess was off, as the in-process request (https://github.com/Kebechet/Api.ToMcp/pull/59) lacked the pairing token MS-ASPNETCORE-TOKEN that UseIISIntegration requires. The tool's request now carries the MCP request's token. A tool called outside an MCP request still gets 400.
- An action without [ApiController] that requires a header a tool never sets, such as Cookie, keeps its tool: MVC runs it with the parameter null rather than answering 400.
